Question: All the students in an algebra class took a \(100\)-point test. Five students scored \(100,\) each student scored at least \(60,\) and the mean score was \(76.\) What is the smallest possible number of students in the class?
Solution:
Let \(n\ge5\) be the number of students. Their mean is \(76\), so their total score is \(76n\). For this class size, the smallest possible total comes from the five scores of \(100\) and scores of \(60\) for everyone else. Therefore
\[
76n\ge5\cdot100+60(n-5)=60n+200.
\]
Subtracting \(60n\) gives \(16n\ge200\), so \(n\ge12.5\). Since a class has a whole number of students, it must have at least \(13\).

To show that \(13\) is possible, use five scores of \(100\), seven scores of \(60\), and one score of \(68\). These are \(13\) scores, all between \(60\) and \(100\), with exactly five perfect scores. Their mean is
\[
\frac{5\cdot100+7\cdot60+68}{13}
=\frac{988}{13}=76.
\]
Thus the smallest possible class size is \(13\), choice D.
